L4: # Applied Algebra
L5: 
L6: Western Governors University
L7: 
L8: ### Course Description and Competencies
L9: #### What to Expect
L10: 
L11: In this course, you will learn how to use algebra to model real-world data. You will use functions, graphs, models, and other math skills to understand the information in authentic and meaningful ways. The material includes readings, interactive graphs, as well as learning checks and quizzes. Learners should complete Applied Probability and Statistics or its equivalent prior to engaging in Applied Algebra.
L12: #### Course Competencies
L13: 
L14: This course covers the following competencies:
L15:   * Analyze graphical depictions of real-world situations using functional properties.
L16:   * Apply linear functions and their properties to real-world problems.
L17:   * Apply polynomial functions and their properties to real-world problems.
L18:   * Apply exponential functions and their properties to real-world problems.
L19:   * Apply logistic functions and their properties to real-world problems.
L20:   * Verify the validity of a given model.
L21:   * Interpret the real-world meaning of various functions based on notation, graphical representations, and data representations.
L22: #### Assessment
L23: 
L24: The assessment provides an opportunity to demonstrate your mastery of the competencies in this course. You may attempt the assessment two times before additional support is necessary. If you require further attempts, please contact your Student Experience Team.

L4: # Organizational Behavior
L5: 
L6: Western Governors University
L7: 
L8: ### Course Description and Competencies
L9: #### What to Expect
L10: 
L11: In this course, you will study individual behavior and the ways in which groups develop. You will also consider the nature of work teams, organizational culture, leadership styles, and performance improvement.
L12: The material is divided into six modules, which focus on the following topics: individuals, groups, team building, culture, leadership, and performance. Knowledge checks and videos appear throughout the course and help you check your learning.
L13: #### Course Competencies
L14: 
L15: This course covers the following competencies:
L16:   * The graduate can describe the effects of specified influences on individual behavior.
L17:   * The graduate can recommend appropriate principles or techniques for guiding the development of a group.
L18:   * The graduate can determine which type of team and team leadership should be used to accomplish a task or project.
L19:   * The graduate analyzes the culture within an organization to determine how to work effectively within that organization.
L20:   * The graduate can analyze leadership theories, methods, and tools in given situations and select the appropriate behavior of the leader.
L21:   * The graduate can develop and recommend how to implement effective performance-evaluation processes.
L22: #### Assessment
L23: 
L24: The assessment provides an opportunity to demonstrate your mastery of the competencies in this course. You may attempt the assessment two times before additional support is necessary. If you require further attempts, please contact your Student Experience Team.

L33: Individuals  |

L35:   * Compare cultural and value frameworks, and their implications for behavior.
L36:   * Explain the factors that influence perception and decision-making.
L37:   * Contrast the three ethical decision criteria.
L38:   * Explain the key elements of motivation and how classic and contemporary motivation theories complement one another.
L39: Groups  |
L40:   * Distinguish between the different types of groups and explain how groups develop and function.
L41:   * Demonstrate how norms, status, and size exert influence on individual behavior.
L42:   * Explain how cohesion and group processes influence group decision-making and effectiveness.
L43:   * Describe types of conflict and outline the negotiation and conflict resolution process.
L44:   * Show how individual differences and social factors influence negotiations.
L45:   * Assess the roles and functions of third-party negotiation in managing conflict.
L46: Team Building  |
L47:   * Analyze the continued popularity of teams in organizations.
L48:   * Contrast the five types of team arrangements.
L49:   * Identify the characteristics of effective teams.
L50:   * Explain how organizations can create effective teams.
L51:   * Decide when to use individuals instead of teams.

L70:   * Describe the leadership role of human resources (HR) in promoting effective, inclusive, and accessible workplaces.

L8: ### Course Description and Competencies
L9: #### What to Expect
L10: In this course, you will work through three modules of content. These are broken down into smaller lessons that help you build communication skills step by step. By studying this material, you will develop skills for identifying the parts of a communication interaction, adapting messages to your audience and setting, using verbal and nonverbal communication effectively, analyzing professional written communication, and evaluating situational factors that can affect a message.
L11: You will also practice recognizing conflict, using interpersonal and cross-cultural communication strategies to support resolution, applying emotional intelligence, and utilizing persuasive communication, presentation skills, and multimedia tools to influence and inform others in thoughtful ways.
L12: #### Course Competencies
L13: 
L14: This course covers the following competencies:
L15: 
L16:   * The learner implements appropriate communication styles based on audience and setting.
L17:   * The learner uses communication strategies for managing conflict.
L18:   * The learner uses communication strategies to influence others.
L19: #### Assessments
L20: 
L21: The assessments provide an opportunity for you to demonstrate your mastery of the competencies in this course. The method of assessment includes three final projects. You must achieve a ranking of Competent on each assessment to pass the course. You may attempt the assessments two times before additional support is necessary. If you require further attempts, please contact your Student Experience Team.
